Messages.Body:
I was using guard duty and managed to have the location burned.

My question is the Guard duty seems to 'remember' the selected location.

If a minion with a Guard Duty and a location, has the location burned, does
the Guard duty kick back into play is a new copy of the same location
returns to play. Reguardless of whether or not you control it?

Second
Do you have to have a location in play to play a guard duty? The Card text
indicates only you name a location, not a location in play.

So is it possible to play guard duty in advance of playing the location and
will the guard duty be effective? Meaning will it acquire the location as a
valid target once the location enters play?

Raille

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Raille wrote:
> I was using guard duty and managed to have the location burned.
>
> My question is the Guard duty seems to 'remember' the selected location.
>
> If a minion with a Guard Duty and a location, has the location burned, does
> the Guard duty kick back into play is a new copy of the same location
> returns to play. Reguardless of whether or not you control it?

No. Effects key on card instance, not card name, by default. (And note that
the "instance" is generally lost if the card goes into the ash heap,
library, hand, or crypt; but not if it is contested or returned to the
uncontrolled region).

> Second
> Do you have to have a location in play to play a guard duty? The Card text
> indicates only you name a location, not a location in play.

The rules cover the "in play" part.
http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/rulebook.html#sec1_6_1 (item #5)

> So is it possible to play guard duty in advance of playing the location and
> will the guard duty be effective? Meaning will it acquire the location as a
> valid target once the location enters play?

No.

--

Messages.Author: The Lasombra

On Sun, 26 Dec 2004 20:07:24 GMT, Daneel <dan...@eposta.hu> wrote:

>> With the current ruling that you can always hunt even if at capacity

>Is this so?

Yes.

Hunting is not restricted to vampires that are short of their
capacity.

See the online rulebook, section 6.1.2.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/

To have a vampire hunt, announce the action and tap the acting
vampire. If the action is successful, move a blood counter to the
acting vampire from the blood bank. If this causes the vampire's blood
to exceed his blood capacity, then (as always) the excess is
immediately returned to the blood bank.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com

I'm not sure LSJ is avoiding it.

Standard LSJ behaviour on such matters is that errata is not issued to
make bad cards stronger. If an issue arises which requires action to
be taken about that card (contradictory wording, say), the action
taken may also make a bad card stronger in the process, but bad cards
don't have errata issued on them just because they're bad.
